observations: Two solar panels leaning against a wall.
The panels have a silver aluminum frame.
The surface is dark, consistent with a monocrystalline or polycrystalline solar cell design.
A watermark 'IZUTECH SOLAR ENERGY' is visible across the center of the image.
The panels appear to be in a warehouse or storage area.

claims.evidence: The watermark is present, but the seller's name is not legible on the panels themselves.

claims.claim: specialize in all solar equipment such as Inverter, panels, charge
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The panels may be used, refurbished, or have physical damage.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification label (usually on the back) showing the model and wattage.

risks.risk: The panels may be non-functional or have significantly reduced output.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter test of the open-circuit voltage (Voc) and short-circuit current (Isc).

risks.risk: The panels may be counterfeit or of a different brand than the watermark suggests.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's label on the back of the panel.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the specification label on the back of the panels.
Photo of the front of the panels to check for cracks or discoloration.
Video of a multimeter test showing the panel's output.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
